why: ACT develops psychological flexibility: making room for difficult experiences while choosing actions connected to what matters.

slides.title: Acceptance & Values
slides.content: Acceptance does not mean liking pain, dismissing symptoms, or abandoning appropriate care. It means reducing the struggle with what cannot be changed in this moment.

slides.title: Psychological Flexibility
slides.content: Learn to notice thoughts and feelings as experiences—not commands that must determine every action.

slides.title: Living with Purpose
slides.content: Focus on meaningful activities and values rather than waiting for pain to disappear

slides.title: Values-Based Action
slides.content: ACT helps you take meaningful action aligned with your values, even when pain is present.

slides.title: Myth vs Fact
slides.content: Myth: Acceptance means giving up. Fact: It frees energy to pursue what matters.

slides.title: Try this today
slides.content: Choose one value—such as connection, health, learning, or independence—and one small action that expresses it today. Adjust the action to your current capacity.
